text:
Lane Hutson was the 62nd pick in 2022, won the Calder in 2024-25, and was Evolving-Hockey's top defenseman in the league last season by wins above replacement. Stéphane Gonzalez now calls him the best defenseman in the NHL, per Dose.ca, and the numbers make it a fair argument. He is playing 25 minutes a night, has 24 points in 24 games, and Montreal takes 57% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, 11.5 points better than without him (expected goals measure the quality of chances). That gap is the biggest thing on his card.

He does it with the puck. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him carrying in on 54% of his entries, rare for a defenseman, and he draws more penalties than he takes. Our range puts him around 83 points by season's end. He was on pace for more than 30 minutes after one period against the Flyers, per The Hockey News. Watch whether the workload starts to cost him late in games.
